observations: Photo 0: a black 12V car battery lying on gravel, top label reads 'SOLITE' with model code 'CMF59015', fitting-date sticker present, terminals are bolt-type, casing is dirty with no visible cracks in this view
Photo 0 background: scrap metal, gravel pile, and what looks like another battery edge at bottom left
Photo 1: a different battery partly in a torn cardboard box, terminals visible, no brand or model text legible, sitting on gravel with a person's sandaled foot nearby for scale
Photo 1 right edge: a third battery visible, black body with red marking, text not legible
No photos show the batteries connected to a charger, multimeter, or load tester
No photos show the underside, sides, or rear of any battery for crack/leak inspection
Seller's own description labels the goods as 'scrap batteries'

claims.evidence: Seller's own framing; photos show no electrical test to confirm whether units are dead, so 'scrap' is taken as the seller's own worst-case description rather than a provable fact

claims.claim: Implied multiple batteries included (at least the Solite unit and the boxed unit, possibly a third)
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show what appear to be different batteries, but no single photo shows a full lineup or count

risks.risk: Battery may be fully dead, sulfated, or internally shorted (common for items labelled 'scrap')
risks.proof: Clip of a multimeter or load tester reading on each terminal pair
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-working scrap, not as a functional battery

risks.risk: Case could be cracked, leaking, or missing acid, which is invisible from the top-down angle shown
risks.proof: Photos of each battery's sides, bottom, and terminal area close-up

risks.risk: Actual number of batteries included in the sale is unclear across the two photos
risks.proof: A single photo showing all units together with a count
risks.if_unproven: priced per single unit only, the one in photo 0, unless seller confirms others are included

risks.risk: Model/capacity sticker (CMF59015, 12V) could be mismatched or swapped from a different unit, common in scrap lots
risks.proof: Clear, unobstructed close-up of the full label including CCA/Ah rating
risks.if_unproven: priced using the visible label as unverified, worst case being a generic small-capacity battery

proof_requests: A load-test or multimeter reading clip for each battery offered
Close-up photos of the sides and bottom of every battery for crack/leak/corrosion check
One photo showing all batteries included in the lot together, counted
A clearer, unobstructed shot of the Solite label's Ah/CCA rating
response.reason: The items are identifiable as a lead-acid car battery (one named: Solite CMF59015, others by type only) explicitly sold as scrap, so they can be priced at worst case as non-working scrap pending any proof of function or condition.
